item.title: Mamdani’s inaugural “rental ripoff” hearing: more conference than brawl
item.description: When Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced his “Rental Ripoff” hearings, he appeared to be advertising a showdown. item.title: NYC’s top deals: British developer offloads UES townhouse for $55M
item.description: There were 252 transactions totaling $493 million filed in New York City records in the 24 hours before 4 p.m. on Thursday, Feb. 26, 2026. 🏆 Residential: The top home sale to hit records was in the Upper East Side. item.title: Hudson Companies files for 300-unit affordable housing project in Gowanus
item.description: The Gowanus rezoning is the gift that keeps on giving in the Brooklyn neighborhood. Hudson Companies filed plans for a 302-unit, 274,000-square-foot residential building at 20 Fifth Street in the Brooklyn neighborhood, PincusCo reported. Chief operating officer Sally Gilliland filed the plans through a limited liability company. item.title: One of Bronx’s “worst landlords” has loan sent to special servicing
item.description: Barry Singer is considered one of the “worst landlords” in New York City by Public Advocate Jumaane Williams. His lenders may not be a fan these days, either. A $39 million mortgage backing a housing portfolio in the Bronx was transferred to special servicing this month after Singer fell behind on payments, Crain’s reported. item.title: Walmart buys its own Farmingdale store for $48M
item.description: Walmart is best known for its sales, but it recently made a noteworthy buy on Long Island: itself. The big-box retailer purchased its location at 965 Broadhollow Road in Farmingdale’s Republic Plaza for $48 million, Commercial Property Executive reported. The acquisition of the 220,000-square-foot building breaks down to $320 per square foot. The seller was N.Y. MetLife Real Estate Investment, which has owned the property since 2014. item.title: Bally’s buys site for Bronx casino from the city
item.description: Casino operator Bally’s is fully in control of its destiny when it comes to developing one of the trio of gaming facilities approved around New York City. The company purchased the parkland for its planned casino and entertainment complex in the Bronx from the city for $156.6 million, the Commercial Observer reported. item.title: “I’m ashamed”: Josh Schuster pleads guilty to Ponzi scheme
item.description: Josh Schuster pleaded guilty to securities fraud Friday and agreed to forfeit $13 million in assets to repay his victims.
